### Using Census Tract's centroid as a unit of analysis




## =============================================================================
## Tour-level Activity Space Construction (Hasanzadeh et al. 2017 approach)
## NHTS 2017 | Caregiver travel with/without children aged 0–9
##
## SAMPLE DEFINITION (matching us_data_processing_1.rmd):
##   Caregivers = adult respondents (age 23–69) in households with at least
##   one child aged 0–9 (numu10inhh >= 1), where:
##     numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD (HH count of ages 0–5, NHTS variable) +
##                  num_5_9   (ages 5–9 counted from perpub roster)
##   Note: NHTS does not roster children under 5; their presence is captured
##   only through YOUNGCHILD. Children aged 5–9 appear in perpub.
##
## ACCOMPANIMENT DEFINITION (matching us_data_processing_1.rmd):
##   PartyNumu10 per trip = acc_0_4 + acc_5_9, where:
##     acc_5_9   = ONTD_P* slots matched to perpub ages 5–9 (directly known)
##     acc_0_4   = HH_ONTD - 1 (self) - known-age companions  (inferred)
##               = unmatched HH companions assumed to be under 5
##   A tour is child_on_tour = TRUE if any trip has PartyNumu10 > 0.
##
## Geographic resolution: Census block-group centroids (TIGER 2017)
## Activity space: MCP = convex hull of buffered stops
##   Home → 500 m buffer; all other destinations → 140 m buffer
## Outcome: log(MCP area in km²) at tour level
##
## Required files:
##   hhctbg.csv    — household home block group (NHTS geographic file)
##   tripctbg.csv  — per-trip destination block group (NHTS geographic file)
##   trippub.csv   — trip public use file (includes HH + person variables)
##   perpub.csv    — person public use file (for child age roster)
## =============================================================================


```{r include=FALSE}
## =============================================================================
## Tour-level Activity Space Construction (Hasanzadeh et al. 2017 approach)
## NHTS 2017 | Caregiver travel with/without children
##
## Geographic resolution: Census block-group centroids (from Census TIGER)
## Activity space: Minimum Convex Polygon (MCP)
##   - Home location buffered 500 m
##   - All other stops buffered 140 m
##   - Union of buffers → MCP (convex hull)
## Outcome: log(area in km²) at the tour level
##
## Required NHTS files (assumed in data_dir):
##   hhctbg.csv      — household home BG
##   tripctbg.csv    — per-trip origin/destination BG
##   trippub.csv     — trip public file (tour ID, child accompaniment flags)
##   hhpub.csv       — household public file (household-level controls)
##   perpub.csv      — person public file (person-level controls)
## =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)   # Census TIGER/Line shapefiles → BG centroids
library(lwgeom)   # convex hull on sf geometry collections

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Paths — edit these
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
data_dir   <- "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/CaregiverActivitySpace/data"          # folder with all NHTS CSVs 
output_dir <- "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/CaregiverActivitySpace/results"            # where results are written

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load NHTS geographic and trip files
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hhctbg  <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "hhctbg.csv"),
                    col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
tripctbg <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "tripctbg.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
trippub  <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "trippub.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
hhpub    <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "hhpub.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
perpub   <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "perpub.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Build household-level child count (numu10inhh)
##    Mirrors the Python logic in us_data_processing_1.rmd:
##      numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD (ages 0–5 from NHTS HH variable)
##                 + num_5_9   (ages 5–9 counted from perpub roster)
##
##    YOUNGCHILD is a household-level variable already in trippub/perpub.
##    Children under 5 are NOT in the perpub roster; YOUNGCHILD captures them.
##    Children 5–9 ARE in the perpub roster via R_AGE_IMP.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# Count ages 5–9 per household from perpub roster
hh_5_9 <- perpub %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(R_AGE)) %>%    # perpub uses R_AGE; R_AGE_IMP is only in trippub
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID) %>%
  summarise(num_5_9 = sum(age >= 5 & age <= 9), .groups = "drop")
 
# YOUNGCHILD: household-level count of ages 0–5, lives in hhpub (not trippub)
hh_youngchild <- hhpub %>%
  select(HOUSEID, YOUNGCHILD) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(YOUNGCHILD = as.integer(YOUNGCHILD),
         YOUNGCHILD = replace_na(YOUNGCHILD, 0L))
 
# Combine: numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD + num_5_9
hh_child_count <- hh_youngchild %>%
  left_join(hh_5_9, by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  mutate(
    num_5_9    = replace_na(num_5_9, 0L),
    numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD + num_5_9
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, YOUNGCHILD, num_5_9, numu10inhh)
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Restrict to caregiver households (numu10inhh >= 1)
##    and adult respondents aged 23–69 (matching your study's age filter)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
caregiver_hh <- hh_child_count %>%
  filter(numu10inhh >= 1) %>%
  pull(HOUSEID)
 
message("Caregiver households (numu10inhh >= 1): ", length(caregiver_hh))
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Build trip core: caregiver households, adult respondents only
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
HOME_CODE <- "01"   # confirmed from data: WHYTO == "01" is home (n = 312,295)
 
trip_core <- trippub %>%
  filter(
    HOUSEID %in% caregiver_hh,
    as.integer(R_AGE_IMP) >= 23,
    as.integer(R_AGE_IMP) <= 69
  ) %>%
  select(
    HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM,
    WHYTO, WHYFROM,
    TRPTRANS, TRVLCMIN, TRPMILES,
    HH_ONTD,          # number of HH members on trip (self-reported, includes self)
    starts_with("ONTD_P"),  # co-traveler person IDs — needed for PartyNumu10
    TDWKND,           # 01 = weekday, 02 = weekend (confirmed from data)
    R_AGE_IMP, R_SEX_IMP,
    DRIVER, WORKER,
    HHVEHCNT, HHFAMINC, HHSIZE, NUMADLT, LIF_CYC,  # YOUNGCHILD comes from hhpub join
    URBRUR, MSACAT, HH_CBSA,
    WTTRDFIN
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    trip_num     = as.integer(TDTRPNUM),
    HH_ONTD      = as.integer(HH_ONTD),
    dest_is_home = WHYTO == HOME_CODE
  ) %>%
  # Drop invalid HH_ONTD values
  filter(!HH_ONTD %in% c(-9L, NA_integer_)) %>%
  arrange(HOUSEID, PERSONID, trip_num)
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Construct tour IDs from trip chains
##    A tour begins each time the previous trip ended at home.
##    default = TRUE so trip 1 always starts tour 1.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
trip_core <- trip_core %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  mutate(
    prev_ended_home = lag(dest_is_home, default = TRUE),
    tour_seq        = cumsum(prev_ended_home),
    tour_id         = paste(HOUSEID, PERSONID, tour_seq, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Compute PartyNumu10 per trip
##    Mirrors the Python logic in us_data_processing_1.rmd:
##
##    acc_5_9   = count of ONTD_P* companions matched to perpub ages 5–9
##    acc_0_4   = (HH_ONTD - 1) - known_age_companions
##              = unmatched HH slots assumed to be under 5 (not in roster)
##    PartyNumu10 = acc_0_4 + acc_5_9  (clipped at 0)
##
##    Note: ONTD_P* contains person IDs of HH members traveling together.
##    "-1" means the slot is empty. Non-HH child companions (NONHHCNT) are
##    not age-identifiable and are excluded, consistent with your prior study.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
ontd_cols <- paste0("ONTD_P", 1:13)
 
# Age lookup from perpub: only ages 5–9 matter here
age_lookup_5_9 <- perpub %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(R_AGE)) %>%    # perpub uses R_AGE; R_AGE_IMP is only in trippub
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, age)
 
# Pivot ONTD_P* to long, match ages, count per trip
ontd_long <- trip_core %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM, HH_ONTD, all_of(ontd_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(ontd_cols),
    names_to  = "slot",
    values_to = "ontd_pid"
  ) %>%
  mutate(ontd_pid = as.character(ontd_pid)) %>%
  filter(!ontd_pid %in% c("-1", "NA", NA_character_))
 
# Join ages for matched companions
ontd_with_age <- ontd_long %>%
  left_join(
    age_lookup_5_9 %>% rename(ontd_pid = PERSONID, comp_age = age),
    by = c("HOUSEID", "ontd_pid")
  )
 
# Per-trip counts
party_counts <- ontd_with_age %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM, HH_ONTD) %>%
  summarise(
    known_age_comp = sum(!is.na(comp_age)),   # all companions with age in roster
    acc_5_9        = sum(!is.na(comp_age) & comp_age >= 5 & comp_age <= 9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # HH_ONTD includes the respondent; subtract 1 to get companions
    hh_comp_total = pmax(HH_ONTD - 1L, 0L),
    # Infer 0–4 as unmatched HH companion slots (not in perpub roster)
    acc_0_4       = pmax(hh_comp_total - known_age_comp, 0L),
    PartyNumu10   = acc_0_4 + acc_5_9
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM, PartyNumu10, acc_0_4, acc_5_9)
 
# Trips with HH_ONTD == 1 (only respondent, no companions) → PartyNumu10 = 0
trip_core <- trip_core %>%
  left_join(party_counts, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID", "TDTRPNUM")) %>%
  mutate(PartyNumu10 = replace_na(PartyNumu10, 0L))
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Tour-level summaries
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
tour_summary <- trip_core %>%
  group_by(tour_id, HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  summarise(
    # Child accompaniment: TRUE if any trip on the tour had PartyNumu10 > 0
    child_on_tour  = any(PartyNumu10 > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Total under-10 child-trips on tour (sum across trips, for descriptives)
    total_u10_trips = sum(PartyNumu10, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_trips        = n(),
    weekend_tour   = any(TDWKND == "02", na.rm = TRUE),  # 02 = weekend (confirmed)
    # Person/HH controls (constant within person)
    age            = as.integer(first(R_AGE_IMP)),
    female         = first(R_SEX_IMP) == "02",             # "02" = female (zero-padded, confirmed from data)
    driver         = first(DRIVER) == "01",
    worker         = first(WORKER) == "01",
    veh_cnt        = as.integer(first(HHVEHCNT)),
    no_vehicle     = first(HHVEHCNT) == "0",              # "0" not "00" (confirmed)
    hh_size        = as.integer(first(HHSIZE)),
    n_adults       = as.integer(first(NUMADLT)),
    income_cat     = first(HHFAMINC),
    lif_cyc        = first(LIF_CYC),
    urbrur         = first(URBRUR),
    msacat         = first(MSACAT),
    wt_trip        = first(WTTRDFIN),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(hh_child_count %>% select(HOUSEID, numu10inhh, num_5_9),
            by = "HOUSEID")
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. Build GEOIDs and download Census BG centroids
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# Home GEOID
hhctbg <- hhctbg %>%
  mutate(
    home_geoid = paste0(
      str_pad(HHSTFIPS,  2, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHCNTYFP,  3, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHCT,      6, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHBG,      1, "left", "0")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, home_geoid)
 
# Destination GEOID (domestic only)
tripctbg <- tripctbg %>%
  filter(DEST_COUNTRY == "USA") %>%
  mutate(
    dest_geoid = paste0(
      str_pad(DEST_ST,   2, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(DEST_CNTY, 3, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(DEST_CT,   6, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(DEST_BG,   1, "left", "0")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM, dest_geoid)
 
# Only caregiver households needed for centroid download
caregiver_trips <- tripctbg %>%
  filter(HOUSEID %in% caregiver_hh)
 
caregiver_homes <- hhctbg %>%
  filter(HOUSEID %in% caregiver_hh)
 
all_geoids  <- union(caregiver_homes$home_geoid, caregiver_trips$dest_geoid)
state_codes <- unique(substr(all_geoids, 1, 2))
 
message("Downloading Census BG centroids for ", length(state_codes), " states ...")
 
bg_sf <- map_dfr(state_codes, function(st) {
  tryCatch(
    block_groups(state = st, year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
      select(GEOID) %>%
      st_centroid(),
    error = function(e) {
      warning("Failed for state ", st, ": ", e$message)
      NULL
    }
  )
})
 
bg_centroids <- bg_sf %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% all_geoids) %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()
 
message("Centroids matched: ", nrow(bg_centroids), " of ", length(all_geoids), " BGs")
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 9. Attach coordinates to trips and homes
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
trip_coords <- trip_core %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM, tour_id) %>%
  left_join(caregiver_trips, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID", "TDTRPNUM")) %>%
  left_join(
    bg_centroids %>% rename(dest_lon = lon, dest_lat = lat),
    by = c("dest_geoid" = "GEOID")
  )
 
home_coords <- caregiver_homes %>%
  left_join(
    bg_centroids %>% rename(home_lon = lon, home_lat = lat),
    by = c("home_geoid" = "GEOID")
  )
 
trip_with_home <- trip_coords %>%
  left_join(home_coords, by = "HOUSEID")
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 10. Compute MCP activity space per tour
##     Home → 500 m buffer; each destination stop → 140 m buffer
##     Union all buffers → convex hull → area in km²
##     CRS: EPSG:5070 (NAD83 Conus Albers, metres, equal area)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
CRS_PROJ <- 5070
 
compute_mcp_area <- function(df_trips, home_lon, home_lat) {
  df_valid <- df_trips %>% filter(!is.na(dest_lon), !is.na(dest_lat))
  if (nrow(df_valid) == 0 || is.na(home_lon) || is.na(home_lat)) return(NA_real_)
 
  home_pt <- st_sfc(st_point(c(home_lon, home_lat)), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(CRS_PROJ)
  dest_pts <- st_as_sf(df_valid, coords = c("dest_lon", "dest_lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(CRS_PROJ)
 
  home_buf  <- st_buffer(home_pt,  dist = 500)
  dest_bufs <- st_buffer(dest_pts, dist = 140)
  all_bufs  <- c(home_buf, st_geometry(dest_bufs))
 
  mcp <- st_convex_hull(st_union(do.call(c, all_bufs)))
  as.numeric(st_area(mcp)) / 1e6
}
 
message("Computing MCP activity spaces ...")
 
tour_spaces <- trip_with_home %>%
  group_by(tour_id, home_lon, home_lat) %>%
  group_modify(~ tibble(
    activity_space_km2 = compute_mcp_area(.x, .y$home_lon, .y$home_lat)
  )) %>%
  ungroup()
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 11. Outlier exclusion (Hasanzadeh et al. 2017 / Granada paper approach)
##     Remove tours > 8 SD above the mean
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
as_mean <- mean(tour_spaces$activity_space_km2, na.rm = TRUE)
as_sd   <- sd(tour_spaces$activity_space_km2,   na.rm = TRUE)
 
tour_spaces <- tour_spaces %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(activity_space_km2),
    activity_space_km2 <= as_mean + 8 * as_sd
  )
 
message("Tours retained after outlier exclusion: ", nrow(tour_spaces))
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 12. Assemble model dataset and log-transform outcome
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
model_data <- tour_spaces %>%
  left_join(tour_summary, by = "tour_id") %>%
  mutate(log_as = log(activity_space_km2))  # no zeros: home 500m buffer guarantees area > 0
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 12b. Recode income into quartiles and clean categorical predictors
##
## HHFAMINC quartile boundaries (based on caregiver subsample distribution):
##   Q1 = 01–05  < $50,000          (~26% of sample)
##   Q2 = 06–07  $50,000–$99,999    (~32%)
##   Q3 = 08–09  $100,000–$149,999  (~23%)
##   Q4 = 10–11  $150,000+          (~19%)
## Observations with HHFAMINC == -7 (refused) or -8 (don't know) are dropped.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
model_data <- model_data %>%
  filter(!income_cat %in% c("-7", "-8")) %>%
  mutate(
    income_num = as.integer(income_cat),
    income_q   = factor(
      case_when(
        income_num %in% 1:5   ~ "Q1",   # < $50,000
        income_num %in% 6:7   ~ "Q2",   # $50,000–$99,999
        income_num %in% 8:9   ~ "Q3",   # $100,000–$149,999
        income_num %in% 10:11 ~ "Q4",   # $150,000+
        TRUE                  ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")  # Q1 = reference
    ),
    urbrur = factor(urbrur)               # ensure factor; R drops one level automatically
  )
 
message("Observations after dropping refused/dk income: ", nrow(model_data))
message("Income quartile distribution:")
print(table(model_data$income_q))
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 13. Descriptive statistics
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
desc_stats <- model_data %>%
  group_by(child_on_tour) %>%
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    mean_km2       = mean(activity_space_km2),
    median_km2     = median(activity_space_km2),
    sd_km2         = sd(activity_space_km2),
    mean_log       = mean(log_as),
    pct_weekend    = mean(weekend_tour),
    mean_numu10_hh = mean(numu10inhh, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups        = "drop"
  )
print(desc_stats)
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 14. Regression models (OLS on log-transformed MCP area)
##
## Key predictor: child_on_tour (TRUE = at least one child aged 0–9
##                traveled on this tour, based on PartyNumu10 > 0)
##
## weekend_tour × child_on_tour interaction tests whether accompaniment
## constrains weekday vs. weekend activity spaces differently
## (motivated by the Granada paper's weekday/weekend divergence finding)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# Model A: child accompaniment + individual controls
model_a <- lm(
  log_as ~ child_on_tour + age + female + driver + no_vehicle + n_trips,
  data = model_data, na.action = na.exclude
)
 
# Model B: + household resource controls
model_b <- lm(
  log_as ~ child_on_tour + age + female + driver + no_vehicle + n_trips +
            numu10inhh + hh_size + income_q + urbrur,
  data = model_data, na.action = na.exclude
)
 
# Model C: weekday/weekend interaction
model_c <- lm(
  log_as ~ child_on_tour * weekend_tour + age + female + driver +
            no_vehicle + n_trips + numu10inhh + hh_size + income_q + urbrur,
  data = model_data, na.action = na.exclude
)
 
summary(model_a)
summary(model_b)
summary(model_c)
 
library(car)
vif(model_b)
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 15. Save
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
write_csv(model_data, file.path(output_dir, "tour_activity_spaces_caregivers.csv"))
message("Done. Saved to ", output_dir)
```


## =============================================================================
## VARIABLE CODING — CONFIRMED FROM DATA
## =============================================================================
## WHYTO == "01"    Home destination           (n = 312,295, dominant code)
## TDWKND == "01"   Weekday (n = 214,306)
## TDWKND == "02"   Weekend (n = 709,266)
## R_SEX_IMP == "2" Female
## HHVEHCNT == "0"  Zero-vehicle household     (not "00")
## YOUNGCHILD       HH count of children 0–5   (in hhpub, NOT trippub)
## numu10inhh       = YOUNGCHILD + roster-counted ages 5–9 from perpub
## PartyNumu10      = acc_0_4 (inferred) + acc_5_9 (roster-matched) per trip
## child_on_tour    = any(PartyNumu10 > 0) across all trips in the tour
## =============================================================================


### ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Choropleth map (county or CBSA level) — most recommended
## Aggregate mean or median activity space area by county or metro area, then fill a US map. 
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

# Aggregate to county level
county_as <- model_data %>%
  left_join(
    hhctbg %>%
      mutate(
        home_geoid  = paste0(
          str_pad(HHSTFIPS,  2, "left", "0"),
          str_pad(HHCNTYFP,  3, "left", "0"),
          str_pad(HHCT,      6, "left", "0"),
          str_pad(HHBG,      1, "left", "0")
        ),
        county_fips = substr(home_geoid, 1, 5)
      ) %>%
      select(HOUSEID, county_fips),
    by = "HOUSEID"
  ) %>%
  group_by(county_fips, child_on_tour) %>%
  summarise(
    median_as_km2 = median(activity_space_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tours       = n(),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_tours >= 5)

# Get county shapefile
counties_sf <- counties(year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(county_fips = GEOID) %>%
  filter(!STATEFP %in% c("02", "15", "72"))   # drop AK, HI, PR for CONUS map

# Join and plot
counties_sf %>%
  left_join(county_as, by = "county_fips") %>%
  filter(!is.na(child_on_tour)) %>%
  mutate(child_on_tour = if_else(child_on_tour,
                                  "With child (0–9)",
                                  "Without child")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = median_as_km2), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name   = "Median activity\nspace (km²)",
    trans  = "log10",
    option = "magma",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ child_on_tour, ncol = 1) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title    = "Caregiver Activity Spaces by Child Accompaniment",
    subtitle = "Median MCP area (km²) by county, NHTS 2017",
    caption  = "Counties with fewer than 5 tours suppressed"
  )
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Dot map of tour centroids, colored by accompaniment
## Plot each tour's home location (BG centroid) as a point, 
## colored by child_on_tour (TRUE/FALSE) and sized or alpha-weighted by 
## activity_space_km2. Shows where caregivers with/without children are 
## located and their space sizes simultaneously.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# After main script: save centroids
saveRDS(bg_centroids, file.path(output_dir, "bg_centroids.rds"))

# In fresh session: reload
bg_centroids <- readRDS(file.path(output_dir, "bg_centroids.rds"))
```


```{r}
## =============================================================================
## Dot Map: Tour Home Locations by Child Accompaniment
## Top 10 Most Populous MSAs, 2017
## Each point = one tour's home BG centroid
## Color = child_on_tour (TRUE/FALSE)
## Size/alpha = activity_space_km2
## =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Top 10 MSA CBSA codes (2017)
##    HH_CBSA in NHTS maps to Census CBSA codes
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top10_msa <- tribble(
  ~HH_CBSA, ~msa_label,
  "35620",  "New York",
  "31080",  "Los Angeles",
  "16980",  "Chicago",
  "19100",  "Dallas–Fort Worth",
  "26420",  "Houston",
  "47900",  "Washington DC",
  "33100",  "Miami",
  "37980",  "Philadelphia",
  "12060",  "Atlanta",
  "14460",  "Boston"
)

# Ordered factor for facet layout (by population rank)
msa_order <- top10_msa$msa_label

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Filter model_data to top 10 MSAs
##    HH_CBSA is already in model_data (pulled from trippub via tour_summary)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
model_data <- model_data %>%
  left_join(
    trippub %>%
      distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, HH_CBSA),
    by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID")
  )

model_data <- model_data %>%
  select(-starts_with("HH_CBSA")) %>%
  left_join(
    trippub %>% distinct(HOUSEID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% select(HOUSEID, HH_CBSA),
    by = "HOUSEID"
  )

plot_data <- model_data %>%
  inner_join(top10_msa, by = "HH_CBSA") %>%
  mutate(msa_label = factor(msa_label, levels = msa_order))

message("Tours in top 10 MSAs: ", nrow(plot_data))
message("By MSA:")
print(plot_data %>% count(msa_label, child_on_tour))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Attach home BG centroid coordinates
##    Rebuild home_geoid from raw hhctbg, then join bg_centroids
##    (bg_centroids was built in the main script; re-use if still in environment,
##     otherwise rebuild from the hhctbg raw file)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rebuild home coords if not already in environment
if (!exists("bg_centroids")) {
  stop("bg_centroids not found. Run the main activity_space_tours.R script first,
       or re-download centroids here.")
}

home_coords_plot <- hhctbg %>%
  mutate(
    home_geoid = paste0(
      str_pad(HHSTFIPS, 2, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHCNTYFP, 3, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHCT,     6, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHBG,     1, "left", "0")
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    bg_centroids %>% rename(home_lon = lon, home_lat = lat),
    by = c("home_geoid" = "GEOID")
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, home_lon, home_lat)

# Verify
home_coords_plot %>% filter(!is.na(home_lon)) %>% nrow()

plot_data <- model_data %>%
  inner_join(top10_msa, by = "HH_CBSA") %>%
  mutate(msa_label = factor(msa_label, levels = msa_order)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(home_lon), !is.na(home_lat))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Get MSA boundary shapefiles for background context
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cbsa_sf <- core_based_statistical_areas(year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% top10_msa$HH_CBSA) %>%
  left_join(top10_msa, by = c("GEOID" = "HH_CBSA")) %>%
  mutate(msa_label = factor(msa_label, levels = msa_order))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Convert plot_data to sf for faceted mapping
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_sf <- plot_data %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("home_lon", "home_lat"), crs = 4326)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Clip points to MSA boundaries (each point shown only in its own MSA panel)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use st_join to confirm each point is within its own CBSA
# (some BG centroids near MSA edges may fall just outside the polygon)
plot_sf_clipped <- plot_sf %>%
  st_join(
    cbsa_sf %>% 
      st_transform(st_crs(plot_sf)) %>%
      select(GEOID, msa_label_shp = msa_label),
    join = st_within
  ) %>%
  filter(as.character(msa_label) == as.character(msa_label_shp) |
           is.na(msa_label_shp))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Activity space size bins for point sizing
##    Log-scale bins so small spaces are still visible
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_sf_clipped <- plot_sf_clipped %>%
  mutate(
    as_bin = cut(
      activity_space_km2,
      breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 20, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("< 1", "1–5", "5–20", "20–100", "> 100"),
      right  = FALSE
    ),
    child_label = if_else(child_on_tour,
                          "With child (0–9)",
                          "Without child")
  )

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. Plot
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Color palette: two distinct, colorblind-safe colors
col_with    <- "#E05C2B"   # warm orange-red = accompanied
col_without <- "#2B7BB9"   # steel blue = unaccompanied

# Point size scale mapped to activity space bins
size_vals <- c("< 1" = 0.4, "1–5" = 0.7, "5–20" = 1.1,
               "20–100" = 1.6, "> 100" = 2.2)

p <- ggplot() +
  # MSA boundary
  geom_sf(
    data  = cbsa_sf,
    fill  = "#F0F0F0",
    color = "#BBBBBB",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  # Tour home locations
  geom_sf(
    data  = plot_sf_clipped,
    aes(color = child_label, size = as_bin),
    alpha = 0.35,
    shape = 16
  ) +
  # Facet by MSA
  facet_wrap(~ msa_label, ncol = 5, scales = "free") +
  # Scales
  scale_color_manual(
    name   = "Child accompaniment",
    values = c("With child (0–9)" = col_with,
               "Without child"    = col_without)
  ) +
  scale_size_manual(
    name   = "Activity space (km²)",
    values = size_vals
  ) +
  # Theme
  theme_void(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 10, color = "#555555", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 7,  color = "#888888", margin = margin(t = 8)),
    strip.text        = element_text(size = 8,  face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 8,  face = "bold"),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.box        = "vertical",
    legend.margin     = margin(t = 8),
    plot.margin       = margin(12, 12, 12, 12)
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 0.9)),
    size  = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Caregiver Tour Activity Spaces in the 10 Largest U.S. Metro Areas",
    subtitle = "Each point = one tour's home location; size = MCP area; color = child accompaniment (ages 0–9)",
    caption  = "Source: NHTS 2017. Activity spaces computed as minimum convex polygons (Hasanzadeh et al. 2017)."
  )
```

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Build one plot per MSA and combine with patchwork
msa_plots <- map(msa_order, function(msa) {
  
  bbox <- cbsa_sf %>% filter(msa_label == msa) %>% st_bbox()
  
  points <- plot_sf_clipped %>% filter(msa_label == msa)
  boundary <- cbsa_sf %>% filter(msa_label == msa)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = boundary, fill = "#F0F0F0", color = "#BBBBBB", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = points,
            aes(color = child_label, size = as_bin),
            alpha = 0.45, shape = 16) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"]),
             expand = TRUE) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name   = "Child accompaniment",
      values = c("With child (0–9)" = "#E05C2B", "Without child" = "#2B7BB9")
    ) +
    scale_size_manual(
      name   = "Activity space (km²)",
      values = c("< 1" = 0.4, "1–5" = 0.7, "5–20" = 1.1, "20–100" = 1.6, "> 100" = 2.2)
    ) +
    labs(title = msa) +
    theme_void(base_family = "sans") +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                     margin = margin(b = 2)),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
})

# Extract shared legend from first plot with legend on
legend_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = plot_sf_clipped %>% filter(msa_label == msa_order[1]),
          aes(color = child_label, size = as_bin), alpha = 0.45, shape = 16) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name   = "Child accompaniment",
    values = c("With child (0–9)" = "#E05C2B", "Without child" = "#2B7BB9")
  ) +
  scale_size_manual(
    name   = "Activity space (km²)",
    values = c("< 1" = 0.4, "1–5" = 0.7, "5–20" = 1.1, "20–100" = 1.6, "> 100" = 2.2)
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 7)) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 0.9)),
         size  = guide_legend(order = 2))

shared_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(legend_plot)

# Combine: 2 rows × 5 cols + legend at bottom
p <- wrap_plots(msa_plots, ncol = 5) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Caregiver Tour Activity Spaces in the 10 Largest U.S. Metro Areas",
    subtitle = "Each point = one tour's home location · size = MCP area · color = child accompaniment (ages 0–9)",
    caption  = "Source: NHTS 2017. Activity spaces computed as minimum convex polygons (Hasanzadeh et al. 2017).",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9,  color = "#555555"),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 7,  color = "#888888")
    )
  )

# Add legend below
final_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p, shared_legend,
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.08)
)

ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "dotmap_top10_msa.png"),

  width = 18, height = 9, dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
```

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Smoothed surface (kernel density or spatial interpolation)
## show where large vs. small activity spaces cluster geographically.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## Figure: Smoothed surface of caregiver activity space areas
## Kernel density + spatial interpolation approach
## Two panels: tours WITH child (0–9) vs. WITHOUT child
## =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(spatstat)    # for kernel-weighted spatial smoothing
library(tigris)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)   # for combining two panels

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Ensure home coordinates are attached to model_data
##    home_lon / home_lat are BG centroid coords (WGS84) used in MCP
##    construction. They live in tour_spaces as grouping vars; carry them
##    through here if not already in model_data.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (!all(c("home_lon", "home_lat") %in% names(model_data))) {
  model_data <- tour_spaces %>%
    select(tour_id, home_lon, home_lat) %>%
    left_join(model_data, ., by = "tour_id")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Prepare point data
##    - Drop missing coordinates
##    - Log-transform activity space (matches model outcome)
##    - Split into two groups
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_data <- model_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(home_lon), !is.na(home_lat), !is.na(activity_space_km2)) %>%
  mutate(
    log_as        = log(activity_space_km2),
    accompaniment = if_else(child_on_tour,
                            "With child (aged 0–9)",
                            "Without child")
  )

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. CONUS bounding box and base map
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONUS_BBOX <- c(xmin = -125, xmax = -66, ymin = 24, ymax = 50)

states_sf <- states(year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!STATEFP %in% c("02", "15", "60", "66", "69", "72", "78")) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Smoothed surface via spatstat
##
## Approach: for each group, create a spatstat ppp (point pattern) with
## log(activity_space_km2) as marks, then use Smooth.ppp() to produce a
## kernel-weighted interpolation of the mark values over a regular grid.
## This gives a surface showing WHERE activity spaces are large vs. small,
## not just where people are dense.
##
## bandwidth (sigma): ~150 km in degrees (~1.35°) — coarse enough to
## produce a readable national surface; adjust downward for regional maps.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SIGMA   <- 1.5      # kernel bandwidth in degrees (~165 km); tune as needed
N_GRID  <- 300      # grid resolution (n × n cells)

# CONUS observation window for spatstat
conus_win <- owin(
  xrange = c(CONUS_BBOX["xmin"], CONUS_BBOX["xmax"]),
  yrange = c(CONUS_BBOX["ymin"], CONUS_BBOX["ymax"])
)

smooth_group <- function(df, win, sigma, ngrid) {
  # Remove points outside window
  df <- df %>%
    filter(
      home_lon >= win$xrange[1], home_lon <= win$xrange[2],
      home_lat >= win$yrange[1], home_lat <= win$yrange[2]
    )

  ppp_obj <- ppp(
    x      = df$home_lon,
    y      = df$home_lat,
    marks  = df$log_as,
    window = win
  )

  # Kernel-weighted smoothing of mark (log activity space)
  # Smooth.ppp computes E[mark | location] via Nadaraya-Watson estimator
  sm <- Smooth(ppp_obj, sigma = sigma, dimyx = c(ngrid, ngrid),
               warn = FALSE)

  # Convert spatstat im object to data frame for ggplot (no stars needed)
  sm_df <- as.data.frame(sm) %>%
    rename(lon = x, lat = y, smooth_log_as = value) %>%
    filter(!is.na(smooth_log_as))

  sm_df
}

message("Smoothing surface for 'With child' group ...")
sm_with <- plot_data %>%
  filter(child_on_tour) %>%
  smooth_group(conus_win, SIGMA, N_GRID) %>%
  mutate(accompaniment = "With child (aged 0–9)")

message("Smoothing surface for 'Without child' group ...")
sm_without <- plot_data %>%
  filter(!child_on_tour) %>%
  smooth_group(conus_win, SIGMA, N_GRID) %>%
  mutate(accompaniment = "Without child")

sm_all <- bind_rows(sm_with, sm_without) %>%
  mutate(
    accompaniment = factor(accompaniment,
                           levels = c("With child (aged 0–9)", "Without child"))
  )

## Shared color scale limits (so panels are directly comparable)
scale_lims <- quantile(sm_all$smooth_log_as, c(0.02, 0.98), na.rm = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Difference surface (with-child minus without-child)
##    Negative values = smaller spaces when child is present (constraint)
##    Positive values = larger spaces when child is present (freedom)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Align grids (they share the same grid because same win + ngrid)
sm_diff <- sm_with %>%
  select(lon, lat, smooth_log_as) %>%
  rename(log_with = smooth_log_as) %>%
  left_join(
    sm_without %>% select(lon, lat, smooth_log_as) %>% rename(log_without = smooth_log_as),
    by = c("lon", "lat")
  ) %>%
  mutate(diff = log_with - log_without)

diff_lim <- max(abs(quantile(sm_diff$diff, c(0.02, 0.98), na.rm = TRUE)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Plot
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Helper: state borders layer
state_borders <- geom_sf(
  data        = states_sf,
  fill        = NA,
  color       = "white",
  linewidth   = 0.25,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

# Panel A: With child
p_with <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(
    data    = sm_with,
    mapping = aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = smooth_log_as),
    interpolate = TRUE
  ) +
  state_borders +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name   = "log(km²)",
    option = "magma",
    limits = scale_lims,
    oob    = scales::squish
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim   = c(CONUS_BBOX["xmin"], CONUS_BBOX["xmax"]),
    ylim   = c(CONUS_BBOX["ymin"], CONUS_BBOX["ymax"]),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(title = "A  With child aged 0–9") +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4))
  )

# Panel B: Without child
p_without <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(
    data    = sm_without,
    mapping = aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = smooth_log_as),
    interpolate = TRUE
  ) +
  state_borders +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name   = "log(km²)",
    option = "magma",
    limits = scale_lims,
    oob    = scales::squish
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim   = c(CONUS_BBOX["xmin"], CONUS_BBOX["xmax"]),
    ylim   = c(CONUS_BBOX["ymin"], CONUS_BBOX["ymax"]),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(title = "B  Without child") +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4))
  )

# Panel C: Difference surface (with minus without)
p_diff <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(
    data    = sm_diff,
    mapping = aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = diff),
    interpolate = TRUE
  ) +
  state_borders +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    name     = "Δ log(km²)\n(with − without)",
    palette  = "RdBu",
    limits   = c(-diff_lim, diff_lim),
    oob      = scales::squish,
    direction = 1   # blue = positive (larger with child), red = negative (smaller)
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim   = c(CONUS_BBOX["xmin"], CONUS_BBOX["xmax"]),
    ylim   = c(CONUS_BBOX["ymin"], CONUS_BBOX["ymax"]),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(title = "C  Difference (with child − without child)") +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4))
  )

## Combine with patchwork
fig <- (p_with | p_without) / p_diff +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Geographic Distribution of Caregiver Activity Spaces",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Kernel-smoothed mean log(MCP area) at caregiver home locations (σ = ",
      SIGMA, "°, ~", round(SIGMA * 111), " km)\n",
      "NHTS 2017 | Caregivers in households with at least one child aged 0–9"
    ),
    caption  = paste0(
      "Activity space = minimum convex polygon of buffered tour stops ",
      "(home: 500 m, other stops: 140 m)\n",
      "Following Hasanzadeh, Broberg & Kyttä (2017)"
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9,  color = "grey40"),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8,  color = "grey50")
    )
  )

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## NOTE ON BANDWIDTH (sigma)
## A larger sigma produces a smoother, more generalised surface.
## For regional zooms (e.g. Northeast corridor, West Coast), reduce sigma
## to ~0.3–0.5 and adjust CONUS_BBOX accordingly.
## For publication, consider also masking the raster to land area only
## using the states_sf polygon to avoid colour bleeding into ocean/sea.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Faceted small multiples by urbanicity (urbrur)
## Not a map per se, but since urbrur is already in THIS model, faceting a 
## choropleth by urban/suburban/rural category makes the accessibility 
## gradient visible without overcrowding a single map.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## FIGURE: County choropleth faceted by urbanicity (URBRUR)
## Shows median caregiver activity space area by county,
## separately for urban / suburban / rural contexts,
## with panels split by child accompaniment (with / without child 0–9)
## =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(scales)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 1. Recode URBRUR to readable labels
##
## NHTS 2017 URBRUR codes:
##   01 = Urban area (>= 50,000 population)
##   02 = Urban cluster (2,500–49,999 population)
##   03 = Rural
## Verify with: model_data %>% count(urbrur)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
model_data_fig <- model_data %>%
  mutate(
    urbrur_label = factor(
      case_when(
        urbrur == "01" ~ "Urban",
        urbrur == "02" ~ "Suburban/\nUrban Cluster",
        urbrur == "03" ~ "Rural",
        TRUE           ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = c("Urban", "Suburban/\nUrban Cluster", "Rural")
    ),
    child_label = if_else(
      child_on_tour,
      "With child (age 0–9)",
      "Without child"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(urbrur_label))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 2. Aggregate median activity space to county × urbrur × child_on_tour
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
county_as <- model_data_fig %>%
  left_join(
    hhctbg %>% mutate(county_fips = substr(home_geoid, 1, 5)),
    by = "HOUSEID"
  ) %>%
  group_by(county_fips, urbrur_label, child_label) %>%
  summarise(
    median_as_km2 = median(activity_space_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tours       = n(),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_tours >= 5)   # suppress unreliable low-count cells

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 3. Get CONUS county shapefile
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
counties_sf <- counties(year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!STATEFP %in% c("02", "15", "72")) %>%   # drop AK, HI, PR
  select(GEOID, geometry) %>%
  rename(county_fips = GEOID)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 4. Join and plot
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
map_data <- counties_sf %>%
  left_join(county_as, by = "county_fips",
            relationship = "many-to-many")

fig_urbrur <- ggplot(map_data %>% filter(!is.na(urbrur_label))) +
  geom_sf(
    data = counties_sf,        # grey base layer for all counties
    fill = "grey92", color = NA
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = median_as_km2),
    color = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name     = "Median activity\nspace (km²)",
    trans    = "log10",
    option   = "magma",
    direction = -1,            # dark = large space
    labels   = label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    na.value = "grey92"
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    urbrur_label ~ child_label   # rows = urbanicity, cols = accompaniment
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    strip.text        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, margin = margin(b = 4)),
    legend.position   = "right",
    legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5,
                                     margin = margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40",
                                     margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey50",
                                     margin = margin(t = 8)),
    plot.margin       = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Caregiver Activity Spaces by Urbanicity and Child Accompaniment",
    subtitle = "Median MCP area (km²) by county | NHTS 2017 | Caregivers with children aged 0–9",
    caption  = "Counties with fewer than 5 tours suppressed (shown in grey).\nActivity space = minimum convex polygon of daily tour destinations."
  )
```
